note: *Ich habe keine Zeit.* *Zeiten* = times (periods), not o'clock.
*Ich gehe zur Arbeit.* = I'm going to work.
Adds *-n* in every case but the nominative: *den Namen*, *dem Namen*.
Looks English, but isn't used in English.
*Wörter* for single words; *Worte* for words said: *ein paar Worte*.
*Viel Glück!* = Good luck! *Glück haben* = to be lucky.
*am Ende* = in the end; *Ende Mai* = at the end of May.
A phone, house or room number; a number in maths is *die Zahl*.
Also *girlfriend*. Feminine nouns in *-in* add *-nen* in the plural.
*die Menschen* = people; also *die Leute*, which has only a plural. Adds *-en* in every case but the nominative.
*Herr Müller* = Mr Müller; *Frau Müller* = Mrs or Ms Müller.
Feminine *die Lehrerin*: most words for people add *-in* for a woman.
*ins Bett gehen* = to go to bed.
One flight of stairs is singular in German: *die Treppe hoch* = up the stairs.
Ordering uses the singular: *Zwei Bier, bitte.*
Fruit in general, always singular. One fruit: *eine Frucht*, or the fruit's name.
*Die Rechnung, bitte!* In a café also *Zahlen, bitte!*
*Das ist mir Wurst.* = I couldn't care less.
*ein Glas Wasser* = a glass of water, without *of*.
*in die Stadt gehen* = to go into town.
The railway station; *der Hauptbahnhof* is the main station.
Also *seat* and *space*: *Ist hier noch Platz?* = Is there room here?
For trains and buses; for the cinema or a concert: *die Karte*.
Every noun in *-tät* is feminine. In speech: *die Uni*.
*zur Post gehen* = to go to the post office.
